_why: John, 12 Oct 2026 (Romans test): a letter's first- and second-person lines are its writer's words, so a summary frames them (“Paul tells the believers in Rome: “…””), never as Yada speaking to the reader. Each letter's writer, readers and one setting line (to whom, and why) are drafted from the tN book introduction quoted in `source`, in plain words. Where tN says the writer gives no name (Hebrews, 1 John) the line says so rather than naming one (rule 4). Nothing here is approved until status is 'approved' (rule 2). Approved by John on 12 Oct 2026.

ROM.author: Paul
ROM.setting: Paul wrote to the believers in Rome to get them ready for his visit, and set out the good news about Jesus in full.
ROM.source: tN Romans intro: “Paul wrote this letter to the Christians in Rome. Paul wanted to get them ready to receive him when he visited them … In this letter Paul most fully described the gospel of Jesus Christ.”

1CO.author: Paul
1CO.setting: Paul wrote from Ephesus to the believers in Corinth, answering their letter and what he had heard about their divisions.
1CO.source: tN 1 Corinthians intro: “While Paul was in Ephesus … People from ‘Chloe’ told Paul about ‘factions’ … and the Corinthian believers wrote a letter to him asking questions.”

2CO.author: Paul
2CO.setting: Paul wrote again to the believers in Corinth, glad they had taken his earlier letter well, and defended his work as an apostle.
2CO.source: tN 2 Corinthians intro: “Paul tells the Corinthians that he is happy that they have responded well to his letter … he continues to defend himself as an apostle.”

GAL.author: Paul
GAL.setting: Paul wrote to the believers in Galatia against teachers who said Christians must keep the law of Moses.
GAL.source: tN Galatians intro: “He wanted to write against the false teachers who said that Christians need to follow the law of Moses.”

EPH.author: Paul
EPH.setting: Paul wrote to the believers in Ephesus about God’s love for them in Christ, and how to live in a way that pleases God.
EPH.source: tN Ephesians intro: “to explain God’s love for them in Christ Jesus … to encourage them to live in a way that pleases God.”

PHP.author: Paul
PHP.setting: Paul wrote from prison to the believers in Philippi to thank them for their gift and to encourage them to rejoice.
PHP.source: tN Philippians intro: “Paul wrote this letter while in prison in Rome … to thank the Philippians for the gift … to encourage them to rejoice.”

COL.author: Paul
COL.setting: Paul wrote to the believers in Colossae, whom he had never met, to encourage them and warn them against false teachers.
COL.source: tN Colossians intro: “he had never met the Colossians in person … he wrote to encourage them and to warn them against false teachers.”

1TH.author: Paul
1TH.setting: Paul had to leave Thessalonica after a few weeks; he wrote to the believers there to strengthen them and teach them more.
1TH.source: tN 1 Thessalonians intro: “persecution forced him to leave after only a few weeks … to make his relationship with the Thessalonians stronger and to teach them more about the gospel.”

2TH.author: Paul
2TH.setting: Paul wrote again to the persecuted believers in Thessalonica, and taught them again about Christ’s return.
2TH.source: tN 2 Thessalonians intro: “He encouraged the believers because they were being persecuted … teach them again about Christ’s return.”

1TI.author: Paul
1TI.setting: Paul wrote to Timothy, whom he had left in Ephesus, about worship, church leaders and false teachers.
1TI.source: tN 1 Timothy intro: “Paul had left Timothy in the city of Ephesus … church worship, qualifications for church leaders, and how to deal with false teachers.”

2TI.author: Paul
2TI.setting: Paul wrote to Timothy knowing he would soon die, to encourage him to keep serving God.
2TI.source: tN 2 Timothy intro: “When Paul wrote this letter, he knew that he would soon die. He wrote to encourage Timothy to continue serving God.”

TIT.author: Paul
TIT.setting: Paul wrote to Titus, who led the churches on Crete, about choosing church leaders and how believers should live.
TIT.source: tN Titus intro: “Titus … was leading the churches on the island of Crete. Paul instructed him about selecting church leaders.”

PHM.author: Paul
PHM.setting: Paul wrote from prison to Philemon, asking him to take back his runaway slave Onesimus as a brother.
PHM.source: tN Philemon intro: “Paul was in a prison … Onesimus had run away … Philemon should accept Onesimus back as a Christian brother.”

HEB.author: The writer
HEB.setting: The writer does not give his name; he wrote to show how great Jesus is and to urge his readers to keep trusting him.
HEB.source: tN Hebrews intro: “Whoever wrote this letter did not include his name … emphasizes the greatness of Jesus and his work and encourages the audience to persevere in trusting him.”

JAS.author: James
JAS.setting: James wrote to suffering believers across the Roman Empire about how to live and treat one another.
JAS.source: tN James intro: “James writes to believers living all over the Roman Empire who are suffering … how believers should live in this world and treat one another.”

1PE.author: Peter
1PE.setting: Peter wrote to Gentile believers who were being persecuted, urging them to keep obeying God.
1PE.source: tN 1 Peter intro: “to encourage Gentile Christians who were being persecuted … to continue obeying God even when they were suffering.”

2PE.author: Peter
2PE.setting: Peter wrote to warn believers about false teachers who said Jesus was taking too long to return.
2PE.source: tN 2 Peter intro: “He warned them about false teachers who were saying Jesus was taking too long to return.”

1JN.author: The writer
1JN.setting: The writer does not give his name; he wrote to correct false teachings and to assure his readers that they were saved.
1JN.source: tN 1 John intro: “The author of this letter does not give his name … to challenge and correct those false teachings … to assure them that they were saved.”

2JN.author: The elder
2JN.setting: The elder wrote to a group of believers to encourage them and warn them about false teachers.
2JN.source: tN 2 John intro: “identifies himself only as ‘the elder’ … to encourage them in their faith and to warn them about false teachers.”

3JN.author: The elder
3JN.setting: The elder wrote to Gaius, asking him to welcome travelling believers and warning him about Diotrephes.
3JN.source: tN 3 John intro: “He instructed Gaius to be hospitable and helpful to fellow believers who were traveling … warned Gaius about a bad leader in the church there named Diotrephes.”

JUD.author: Jude
JUD.setting: Jude wrote to warn believers against false teachers.
JUD.source: tN Jude intro: “Jude wrote this letter to warn believers against false teachers.”
